name: Dominican Republic
snapshot: The Caribbean's fastest-growing big economy, run by Luis Abinader, whose hard line on Haitian migrants is popular at home and criticised abroad.
culture: Merengue and bachata, once considered lower-class music, are now national treasures and global exports. Baseball is a passion and a pipeline: more Major League players come from the Dominican Republic than from any other country outside the US. Santo Domingo's colonial zone holds the oldest cathedral in the Americas.
society: Tourism, free trade zones, remittances and mining have driven decades of strong growth. The country shares Hispaniola with Haiti, and Haitian workers are crucial to construction and farming, but mass deportations of Haitians rose sharply under Abinader. A 2025 nightclub roof collapse in Santo Domingo killed over 200 people.
baseline: Luis Abinader won re-election in 2024 with 57 percent and cannot run again in 2028. He has built a border wall with Haiti and stepped up deportations, while promoting a constitutional reform to block future presidents from changing term limits.
